resources.string: Blurp

Blurp frosts the folding half of your screen while you open and close your phone, everywhere including the lock screen. It only draws a blur on top of the screen. It doesn\'t read, collect or share anything on your screen.
Blurp

Blurp frosts the half of your screen that moves while you fold, in every app and on the lock screen. Only Android\'s Accessibility service lets an app lay a layer over the lock screen and every other app, so Blurp needs it.\n\nBlurp uses it only to draw that frost. It doesn\'t read what\'s on your screen or what you type, and it doesn\'t collect or share any data. It has no internet access.
I understand and allow Blurp to use the Accessibility service
Continue
Turn on Blurp
Tap Open Settings, then Installed apps and Blurp, and switch Blurp on. Then come back.
Open Settings
Open App info
Android guards apps installed from a download, so switching Blurp on takes three steps:
Tap Open Settings, then Installed apps and Blurp. Android answers “App was denied access”. Tap Close and come back here.
Tap Open App info, then ⋮ at the top right, and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Confirm if Android asks, then come back here.
Tap Open Settings again, then Installed apps and Blurp. Switch Blurp on and tap Allow.
Next step
Settings, Accessibility: Installed apps, the row under Accessibility shortcuts.
Blurp\'s App info with the ⋮ menu open: Allow restricted settings, at the top right.
Close your phone, then open it
That\'s it. Works everywhere, even on the lock screen.
